data.prompt: Lock in that AgentSupervisor::spawn_child is the sole production entry point for spawning in Phase 6. AgentEffect::SpawnAgent remains a future data shape for core-driven triggers (e.g., a future agent.spawn tool). AgentRunner::dispatch_effects' SpawnAgent match arm stays a stub/warning with a tracing::warn! (only reachable if something else constructs the effect, which nothing does yet). Document this decision as a comment/docstring convention to apply in all downstream tasks (T6.1–T6.14). This is a decision-only checkpoint with no code changes; flag it before proceeding to T6.1 if the assumption is incorrect for your architecture.

data.name: Implement budget enforcement primitives (max_children/max_depth)
data.prompt: Extend harness-core/src/budget.rs with two new methods on the BudgetCheck trait: check_children(current_children: u32) -> Result<(), BudgetError> and check_depth(current_depth: u32) -> Result<(), BudgetError>. Add corresponding BudgetError variants: TooManyChildren { limit, current } and MaxDepthExceeded { limit, current }. Implement both methods on AgentBudget, returning Err if current >= limit, Ok(()) if within bounds or if the corresponding Option is None (unbounded). Add unit tests in budget.rs' existing #[cfg(test)] module: (a) check_children passes at current < limit, rejects at current == limit; (b) check_depth same behavior; (c) both return Ok when Option::None (unbounded case).

data.name: Extend capability derivation to full AgentCapabilities (tools + spawning + depth)
data.prompt: Add a new public method derive_child_agent_capabilities to harness-core/src/capabilities.rs, distinct from the existing derive_child_capabilities (which stays untouched and is reused internally). The new method accepts &ToolInheritance, Option<WorkspaceCapabilities>, and Option<BackendCapabilities>, returning Result<AgentCapabilities, CapabilityError>. Implement non-escalation enforcement: child.can_spawn_agents stays false if parent.can_spawn_agents is false; child.max_child_depth is decremented from parent (Some(d) -> Some(d-1), Some(0) -> None to block grandchildren; None stays None). Reuse existing derive_child_capabilities internally for tool derivation. Add unit tests: (a) parent with can_spawn_agents=false yields child with can_spawn_agents=false; (b) parent max_child_depth=Some(1) yields child max_child_depth=Some(0) and can_spawn_agents=false (grandchildren blocked); (c) ToolInheritance::Subset([fs.read]) from parent with fs.read (delegatable) + shell.exec (not delegatable) yields child toolset with only fs.read.

data.name: Add depth tracking to AgentState and Agent::new
data.prompt: Add pub depth: u32 field to AgentState in harness-core/src/agent_state.rs (0 for root, parent.depth+1 for children). Update Agent::new constructor signature in harness-core/src/agent.rs to require depth: u32 as an explicit parameter (no default value, so the compiler catches missed depth threading). Root agents pass depth=0; children pass parent.depth+1 (enforcement happens in runtime supervisor, not core). Update all existing test helpers in agent.rs and transitions.rs to pass depth=0 so existing tests still compile without modification. Add new test asserting Agent::new(..., depth=3, ...).state.depth == 3. The depth field is read-only from core's perspective (core never enforces depth limits; that's runtime supervisor's job in T6.4).

data.name: Implement AgentSupervisor core structure and spawn budget/depth gating
data.prompt: Create new file crates/harness-runtime/src/agent_supervisor.rs. Implement AgentSupervisor struct holding session_id, session_cancel, agents: RwLock<HashMap<AgentId, AgentHandle>>, and children_of: RwLock<HashMap<AgentId, Vec<AgentId>>>. Define AgentHandle holding parent_id, depth, cancel, and join handle. Define SupervisorError enum with variants Budget(#[from] BudgetError), Capability(#[from] CapabilityError), ParentNotFound(AgentId). Implement constructor fn new(), and method max_children_depth_check(parent_id, parent_depth, parent_budget) that (a) counts current children from children_of, (b) calls parent_budget.check_children(current), (c) calls parent_budget.check_depth(parent_depth), (d) returns Result<(), SupervisorError>. Implement register(parent_id, child_id, depth, cancel, join) and deregister(child_id) for registry management. Add pub mod agent_supervisor; to harness-runtime/src/lib.rs. Add unit test: construct supervisor, register 2 fake children under one parent with max_children=2, assert 3rd max_children_depth_check call returns Err(SupervisorError::Budget(BudgetError::TooManyChildren)) before any task is spawned.

data.name: Implement full spawn flow: AgentSupervisor::spawn_child (8-step)
data.prompt: Add public async method spawn_child to AgentSupervisor. Accept parent: &Agent, parent_backend: Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>, integration_registry: &IntegrationRegistry, tool_registry: Arc<dyn ToolRegistry>, workspace: Arc<dyn Workspace>, event_sink: Arc<dyn EventSink>, scheduler: Arc<Scheduler>, and spec: SpawnAgentSpec. Implement the exact 8-step flow from spec Section 21: (1) call max_children_depth_check to gate; (2) resolve backend (Inherit -> parent_backend.clone(), Explicit TBD in T6.6); (3) call parent.capabilities.derive_child_agent_capabilities(&spec.tools, None, None) for tool/spawning/depth inheritance; (4) resolve workspace (all modes TBD in T6.8/T6.10, stub to workspace.clone() for now); (5) use spec.budget as-is; (6) create child_cancel = self.session_cancel.child_token(); (7) construct new Agent with depth=parent.state.depth+1, create AgentTask + AgentRunner; (8) spawn async task via tokio::spawn() and call self.register(). Return AgentId on success. Add integration test: spawn child with ToolInheritance::Subset([fs.read]) from parent with fs.read (delegatable) + shell.exec (not delegatable); assert child.capabilities.tools contains exactly [fs.read].

data.name: Implement backend inheritance/override resolution via IntegrationRegistry
data.prompt: In harness-runtime/src/agent_supervisor.rs, replace the BackendPolicy::Explicit stub arm in spawn_child (currently parent_backend.clone()) with real resolution. Call integration_registry.create(&reference.integration, reference_to_config(reference)).await to instantiate a fresh Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend> independent of parent's. Add SupervisorError::Integration(#[from] IntegrationError) variant. Ensure child always receives its own backend instance. Add acceptance test: spawn child with BackendPolicy::Explicit referencing a second registered FakeBackend (via FakeIntegrationFactory in test), verify child executes against that backend's scripted events, not parent's.

data.name: Implement SpawnMode (AwaitResult vs Concurrent)
data.prompt: In harness-runtime/src/agent_supervisor.rs, define SpawnOutcome enum: Awaited(AgentResult) | Detached(AgentId). Add public async method spawn_and_drive that wraps spawn_child. After spawn_child returns child_id, check spec.mode: if SpawnMode::Concurrent return Ok(SpawnOutcome::Detached(child_id)) immediately; if SpawnMode::AwaitResult call await_child(child_id) to join the spawned task and retrieve final AgentResult via oneshot channel, return Ok(SpawnOutcome::Awaited(result)). Modify AgentHandle to include oneshot::Sender<AgentResult> for result capture. Add test: spawn two children with AwaitResult, assert calling task genuinely blocks (use a channel to verify parent effect processing pauses until both await_child returns). Add separate test: spawn children with Concurrent, assert spawn_and_drive returns Detached immediately while children continue executing in background.

data.name: Implement workspace isolation: ReadOnlyWorkspace and SnapshotWorkspace
data.prompt: In harness-workspace/src/workspace.rs, promote the existing stub IsolatedWorkspace to a hardened ReadOnlyWorkspace (use pub type ReadOnlyWorkspace = IsolatedWorkspace; to reuse without renaming, limiting surface). Implement new SnapshotWorkspace struct wrapping FsWorkspace rooted at temp directory. Add async fn create(source_root: &Path) -> Result<Self, WorkspaceError> that recursively copies all files from source_root to std::env::temp_dir()/harness-snapshot-{uuid}, returning Self. Implement Workspace trait for both: ReadOnly delegates ops to inner (rejecting write with WorkspaceError::Isolated); Snapshot delegates to inner FsWorkspace on temp root. Add helper fn copy_dir_recursive(src: &Path, dst: &Path) for plain recursive copy (doc's chosen default, no COW). Add unit tests: (a) ReadOnly test calls write, verifies WorkspaceError::Isolated rejection; (b) Snapshot test: child writes to snapshot root, parent reads original via separate FsWorkspace, confirming edits are isolated.

data.name: Implement NewWorktree policy with git2
data.prompt: Create crates/harness-workspace/src/worktree.rs. Add git2 dependency to root Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies] for version consistency. Implement WorktreeWorkspace struct holding inner: FsWorkspace (rooted at new worktree), worktree_path, and repo_root. Add async fn create(repo_root: &Path, branch_hint: &str) -> Result<Self, WorkspaceError> wrapping git2 calls in tokio::task::spawn_blocking (synchronous). Call git2::Repository::open(repo_root)?.worktree(branch_hint, &worktree_path, None)? to create real git checkout. Implement Workspace trait delegating to inner. Add WorkspaceError::Git(String) variant and from_git helper in workspace.rs. Add module pub mod worktree; to harness-workspace/src/lib.rs. Add unit test: create temp git repo, spawn WorktreeWorkspace, child writes+commits in worktree, verify commit does not appear on parent's branch (git log on repo_root), verify worktree is real directory on disk.

data.prompt: In harness-runtime/src/agent_supervisor.rs, replace the child_workspace = workspace.clone() stub in spawn_child with full match: Inherit => workspace.clone(), ReadOnly => Arc::new(ReadOnlyWorkspace::new(workspace.clone())), Snapshot => Arc::new(SnapshotWorkspace::create(workspace.root()).await?), NewWorktree => Arc::new(WorktreeWorkspace::create(workspace.root(), &child_id.to_string()).await?). Add four acceptance tests in agent_supervisor.rs test module (one per policy) exercising full spawn_child path, verifying AgentRunner actually receives the expected workspace variant (can check via a spy on runner state or via observable behavior).

data.name: Fix child completion/failure: wire usage rollup and status resumption
data.prompt: In harness-core/src/transitions.rs, extend child_completed to populate parent.usage from result.usage (currently discarded). Add private fn bridge_usage_summary(protocol: &harness_protocol::usage::AgentUsageSummary) -> harness_core::usage::AgentUsageSummary to convert between the two types (protocol's AgentUsageMetrics to core's ModelUsage). In harness-core/src/agent.rs, add child_usage: HashMap<AgentId, harness_core::usage::AgentUsageSummary> field to UsageLedger; implement add_child_summary(agent_id, summary) method. Update child_completed to call self.usage.add_child_summary(agent_id, bridge_usage_summary(&result.usage)). Also fix status transition: if self.state.children.is_empty() && status == WaitingForChildren, transition to Idle and emit StateChanged event. Update child_failed similarly. Add unit test: agent in WaitingForChildren with two pending children; first ChildCompleted keeps status WaitingForChildren; second transitions to Idle and emits StateChanged; verify both children's usage is stored in ledger for later retrieval.

data.name: Wire real ChildCompleted/ChildFailed delivery from runtime supervisor to parent
data.prompt: In harness-runtime/src/agent_supervisor.rs, after a child's AgentRunner completes (join handle resolves or oneshot fires), retrieve final AgentResult/AgentError via new AgentRunner::take_final_result() method (add to agent_runner.rs: store last FinishRun outcome when dispatch_effects sees it, return via take_final_result: pub fn take_final_result(&mut self) -> Option<Result<AgentResult, AgentError>>). In the spawned task's completion handler (after runner.run() returns), match take_final_result(): Ok(result) -> send AgentCommand::ChildCompleted to parent_commands_tx, Err(error) -> send AgentCommand::ChildFailed. Call self.deregister(child_id) after sending. Add acceptance test matching spec Section 73: root spawns child via spawn_and_drive, verify session event stream shows AgentAdded A1 -> status updates -> tool activity -> A1 completed -> A usage updated in exact order.

data.name: Implement usage aggregation: inclusive_usage query without parent mutation
data.prompt: In harness-runtime/src/agent_supervisor.rs, expose public method inclusive_usage(&self, agent: &Agent) -> harness_core::usage::AgentUsageSummary. Call harness_core::usage::compute_agent_usage_summary with agent.usage.records (self usage) and vec![child_usage.values()...] from the HashMap populated by T6.11 (already separate, no mutation of parent ledger guaranteed by design). Return full AgentUsageSummary with self_usage, descendant_usage, inclusive_usage correctly computed. Add unit test: after two children each report usage via T6.12 flow, call inclusive_usage(&root), verify inclusive_usage.inclusive_usage == self_usage + sum(children's self_usage) numerically.

data.name: Implement Phase 6 concurrency test: root spawns two concurrent children
data.prompt: Create crates/harness-runtime/tests/subagents.rs following exact conventions from tests/concurrency.rs: use FakeBackend, FakeToolRegistry, FakeWorkspace, polling-with-timeout (no raw sleeps). Implement test_root_spawns_two_concurrent_children: root spawns two children via spawn_and_drive(SpawnMode::Concurrent), both children stream scripted FakeBackend events concurrently, root's event subscription observes both children's AgentAdded and ChildAgentCompleted events in correct order, verify both complete without blocking root. Implement test_heterogeneous_backends (requires T6.6): root on one FakeBackend, one child on second registered FakeBackend via BackendPolicy::Explicit(reference), verify child executes against its own backend's events. Ensure all assertions use explicit channel/event synchronization, never brittle sleep-based checks. Both tests must pass deterministically in CI (tolerate CI scheduling jitter via proper synchronization, not via loose timing).

pub struct AgentSupervisor {
    session_id: SessionId,
    session_cancel: SessionCancellation,
    agents: RwLock<HashMap<AgentId, AgentHandle>>,
    children_of: RwLock<HashMap<AgentId, Vec<AgentId>>>,
}

struct AgentHandle {
    parent_id: Option<AgentId>,
    depth: u32,
    cancel: CancellationToken,
    join: JoinHandle<()>,
}

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum SupervisorError {
    #[error("budget: {0}")]
    Budget(#[from] BudgetError),
    #[error("capability: {0}")]
    Capability(#[from] CapabilityError),
    #[error("parent agent not found: {0:?}")]
    ParentNotFound(AgentId),
}

impl AgentSupervisor {
    pub fn new(session_id: SessionId, session_cancel: SessionCancellation) -> Self {
        Self {
            session_id,
            session_cancel,
            agents: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
            children_of: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
        }
    }

    pub async fn max_children_depth_check(
        &self,
        parent_id: AgentId,
        parent_depth: u32,
        parent_budget: &AgentBudget,
    ) -> Result<(), SupervisorError> {
        let children = self.children_of.read().await;
        let current = children.get(&parent_id).map(|v| v.len()).unwrap_or(0) as u32;
        parent_budget.check_children(current)?;
        parent_budget.check_depth(parent_depth)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    async fn register(&self, parent_id: Option<AgentId>, child_id: AgentId, depth: u32, cancel: CancellationToken, join: JoinHandle<()>) {
        let mut agents = self.agents.write().await;
        let mut children = self.children_of.write().await;
        agents.insert(child_id, AgentHandle { parent_id, depth, cancel, join });
        if let Some(pid) = parent_id {
            children.entry(pid).or_insert_with(Vec::new).push(child_id);
        }
    }

    async fn deregister(&self, child_id: AgentId) {
        let mut agents = self.agents.write().await;
        if let Some(handle) = agents.remove(&child_id) {
            if let Some(pid) = handle.parent_id {
                let mut children = self.children_of.write().await;
                if let Some(v) = children.get_mut(&pid) {
                    v.retain(|c| *c != child_id);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

//! Deterministic budget checks for protocol budget values.

use harness_protocol::usage::{AgentBudget, Cost, ModelUsage};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum BudgetError {
    #[error("Usage exceeds budget: {0}")]
    Exceeded(String),
    #[error("Cost exceeds budget")]
    CostExceeded,
    #[error("max_children ({limit}) exceeded: already have {current}")]
    TooManyChildren { limit: u32, current: u32 },
    #[error("max_depth ({limit}) exceeded: current depth is {current}")]
    MaxDepthExceeded { limit: u32, current: u32 },
}

/// Extension methods for checking an [`AgentBudget`] without violating Rust's orphan rules.
pub trait BudgetCheck {
    fn check_usage(&self, usage: &ModelUsage) -> Result<(), BudgetError>;
    fn check_cost(&self, cost: &Cost) -> Result<(), BudgetError>;
    fn check_children(&self, current_children: u32) -> Result<(), BudgetError>;
    fn check_depth(&self, current_depth: u32) -> Result<(), BudgetError>;
}

impl BudgetCheck for AgentBudget {
    fn check_usage(&self, usage: &ModelUsage) -> Result<(), BudgetError> {
        if let (Some(limit), Some(actual)) = (self.max_total_tokens, usage.total_tokens.value()) {
            if actual > limit {
                return Err(BudgetError::Exceeded(format!(
                    "total tokens {actual} exceeds limit {limit}"
                )));
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn check_cost(&self, cost: &Cost) -> Result<(), BudgetError> {
        if let (Some(limit), Some(actual)) = (self.max_cost_usd, cost.amount_usd) {
            if actual > limit {
                return Err(BudgetError::CostExceeded);
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn check_children(&self, current_children: u32) -> Result<(), BudgetError> {
        if let Some(limit) = self.max_children {
            if current_children >= limit {
                return Err(BudgetError::TooManyChildren { limit, current: current_children });
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn check_depth(&self, current_depth: u32) -> Result<(), BudgetError> {
        if let Some(limit) = self.max_depth {
            if current_depth >= limit {
                return Err(BudgetError::MaxDepthExceeded { limit, current: current_depth });
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

    use harness_protocol::usage::{AgentBudget, Cost, ModelUsage, UsageValue};
    use rust_decimal::Decimal;

    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn usage_limit_is_enforced() {
        let budget = AgentBudget { max_total_tokens: Some(100), ..Default::default() };
        assert!(budget.check_usage(&ModelUsage {
            total_tokens: UsageValue::new(Some(101)),
            ..Default::default()
        }).is_err());
        assert!(budget.check_usage(&ModelUsage {
            total_tokens: UsageValue::new(None),
            ..Default::default()
        }).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn cost_limit_is_enforced() {
        let budget = AgentBudget {
            max_cost_usd: Some(Decimal::new(10, 0)),
            ..Default::default()
        };
        assert!(budget.check_cost(&Cost {
            amount_usd: Some(Decimal::new(11, 0)),
            source: None,
        }).is_err());
        assert!(budget.check_cost(&Cost::default()).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn children_limit_is_enforced() {
        let budget = AgentBudget { max_children: Some(3), ..Default::default() };
        // Below the limit passes.
        assert!(budget.check_children(2).is_ok());
        // At the limit is rejected.
        assert_eq!(
            budget.check_children(3),
            Err(BudgetError::TooManyChildren { limit: 3, current: 3 })
        );
        // Above the limit is rejected.
        assert!(budget.check_children(4).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn depth_limit_is_enforced() {
        let budget = AgentBudget { max_depth: Some(3), ..Default::default() };
        // Below the limit passes.
        assert!(budget.check_depth(2).is_ok());
        // At the limit is rejected.
        assert_eq!(
            budget.check_depth(3),
            Err(BudgetError::MaxDepthExceeded { limit: 3, current: 3 })
        );
        // Above the limit is rejected.
        assert!(budget.check_depth(4).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn unbounded_limits_pass() {
        let budget = AgentBudget::default();
        // Unbounded children and depth always pass.
        assert!(budget.check_children(0).is_ok());
        assert!(budget.check_children(1000).is_ok());
        assert!(budget.check_depth(0).is_ok());
        assert!(budget.check_depth(1000).is_ok());
    }
}

fn child_completed(&mut self, agent_id: AgentId, result: AgentResult) -> Vec<AgentEffect> {
    self.state.children.retain(|c| *c != agent_id);

    if self.state.children.is_empty() && self.state.status == AgentStatus::WaitingForChildren {

        effects.push(AgentEffect::Emit {
            event: AgentEvent::StateChanged {
                from: AgentStatus::WaitingForChildren,
                to: AgentStatus::Idle,

}

impl AgentCapabilities {
    pub fn derive_child_agent_capabilities(
        &self,
        inheritance: &ToolInheritance,
        workspace_override: Option<WorkspaceCapabilities>,
        backend_override: Option<BackendCapabilities>,
    ) -> Result<AgentCapabilities, CapabilityError> {
        let tools = self.derive_child_capabilities(inheritance)?;

        let max_child_depth = match (self.max_child_depth, ) {
            (Some(d),) if d == 0 => None, // parent forbids further descent
            (Some(d),) => Some(d - 1),
            (None,) => None,
        };

        Ok(AgentCapabilities {
            tools,
            can_spawn_agents: self.can_spawn_agents && max_child_depth != Some(0),
            max_child_depth,
            workspace: workspace_override.unwrap_or_else(|| self.workspace.clone()),
            backend: backend_override.unwrap_or_else(|| self.backend.clone()),
        })
    }
}

/// Controls how workspace instances observe each other's writes.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub enum WorkspaceMode {
    /// Multiple handles on the same root see each other's writes (default).
    #[default]
    Shared,
    /// Writes from one handle are invisible to others (stub — returns errors).
    Isolated,
}

#[derive(thiserror::Error, Debug)]
pub enum WorkspaceError {
    #[error("IO error: {0}")]
    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),

pub struct SnapshotWorkspace {
    inner: crate::FsWorkspace,
    _origin: Arc<dyn Workspace>,
}

impl SnapshotWorkspace {
    /// Create a new snapshot of `source_root` rooted at
    /// `<temp_dir>/harness-snapshot-<uuid>`.
    pub async fn create(source_root: &Path) -> Result<Self, WorkspaceError> {
        let temp_root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "harness-snapshot-{}",
            uuid::Uuid::new_v4()
        ));
        copy_dir_recursive(source_root, &temp_root).await?;
        Ok(Self {
            inner: crate::FsWorkspace::new(temp_root),
            _origin: Arc::new(crate::FsWorkspace::new(source_root.to_path_buf())),
        })
    }
}

    }

        self.inner.write(relative_path, content).await
    }

        self.inner.search(query).await
    }

    async fn list_files(&self, max_depth: usize) -> Result<Vec<FileInfo>, WorkspaceError> {
        self.inner.list_files(max_depth).await
    }
}

/// Recursively copy the contents of `src` into `dst` (a plain, non-COW copy).
/// The destination directory is created if missing.
async fn copy_dir_recursive(src: &Path, dst: &Path) -> Result<(), WorkspaceError> {
    tokio::fs::create_dir_all(dst).await?;
    let mut entries = tokio::fs::read_dir(src).await?;
    while let Some(entry) = entries.next_entry().await? {
        let file_type = entry.file_type().await?;
        let src_path = entry.path();
        let dst_path = dst.join(entry.file_name());
        if file_type.is_dir() {
            copy_dir_recursive(&src_path, &dst_path).await?;
        } else {
            tokio::fs::copy(&src_path, &dst_path).await?;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub async fn spawn_child(
    &self,
    parent: &Agent,
    parent_backend: Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>,
    integration_registry: &IntegrationRegistry,
    tool_registry: Arc<dyn ToolRegistry>,
    workspace: Arc<dyn Workspace>,
    event_sink: Arc<dyn EventSink>,
    scheduler: Arc<Scheduler>,
    spec: SpawnAgentSpec,
) -> Result<AgentId, SupervisorError> {
    // 1. gating
    self.max_children_depth_check(parent.id, parent.state.depth, &parent.budget).await?;

    // 2. backend resolution
    let backend = match &spec.backend {
        BackendPolicy::Inherit => parent_backend.clone(),
        BackendPolicy::Explicit(_reference) => parent_backend.clone(), // TBD in T6.6
    };

    // 3. capability/tool inheritance
    let capabilities = parent.capabilities.derive_child_agent_capabilities(&spec.tools, None, None)?;

    // 4. workspace resolution
    let child_workspace = workspace.clone(); // TBD in T6.10

    // 5. budget = spec.budget as-is
    // 6. cancellation
    let child_cancel = self.session_cancel.child_token();

    // 7/8. construct Agent + spawn task
    let child_id = AgentId::new();
    let child_agent = Agent::new(child_id, parent.session_id, Some(parent.id),
        spec.role.clone().unwrap_or_default(), BackendBinding::from(&backend),
        capabilities, spec.budget.clone(), parent.state.depth + 1);

    let (task, _tx) = AgentTask::new(child_id);
    let mut runner = AgentRunner::new(child_agent, task, backend, tool_registry, event_sink, child_cancel.clone(), Default::default(), scheduler);
    let join = tokio::spawn(async move { runner.run().await; });

    self.register(Some(parent.id), child_id, parent.state.depth + 1, child_cancel, join).await;
    Ok(child_id)
}

//! Hierarchical agent supervision for a single session.
//!
//! The [`AgentSupervisor`] owns the live registry of running agents for one
//! session: which agent is a child of which parent, each agent's nesting
//! depth, its cancellation token, and its spawned task handle. It is the sole
//! production entry point for spawning sub-agents in this phase (spec §21);
//! core-driven triggers such as `AgentEffect::SpawnAgent` remain a reserved
//! data shape for a future `agent.spawn` tool.
//!
//! Spawning is gated by [`max_children_depth_check`](AgentSupervisor::max_children_depth_check),
//! which enforces the parent's `max_children`/`max_depth` budget **before** any
//! child task is created.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use harness_core::budget::{BudgetCheck, BudgetError};
use harness_core::capabilities::CapabilityError;
use harness_protocol::ids::{AgentId, SessionId};
use harness_protocol::usage::AgentBudget;
use tokio::sync::RwLock;
use tokio::task::JoinHandle;
use tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken;

use crate::cancellation::SessionCancellation;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AgentHandle
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Bookkeeping for a single live agent tracked by the supervisor.
struct AgentHandle {
    parent_id: Option<AgentId>,
    depth: u32,
    cancel: CancellationToken,
    join: JoinHandle<()>,
}

/// Errors surfaced while supervising agent spawning and lifecycle.
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum SupervisorError {
    #[error("budget: {0}")]
    Budget(#[from] BudgetError),
    #[error("capability: {0}")]
    Capability(#[from] CapabilityError),
    #[error("parent agent not found: {0:?}")]
    ParentNotFound(AgentId),
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AgentSupervisor
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The live registry of agents for a single session.
pub struct AgentSupervisor {
    session_id: SessionId,
    session_cancel: SessionCancellation,
    /// Child → handle registry (every tracked agent).
    agents: RwLock<HashMap<AgentId, AgentHandle>>,
    /// Parent → direct child IDs, used for `max_children` accounting.
    children_of: RwLock<HashMap<AgentId, Vec<AgentId>>>,
}

impl AgentSupervisor {
    /// Creates an empty supervisor scoped to a session.
    pub fn new(session_id: SessionId, session_cancel: SessionCancellation) -> Self {
        Self {
            session_id,
            session_cancel,
            agents: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
            children_of: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
        }
    }

    /// Enforces the parent's `max_children` and `max_depth` budget **before**
    /// a child task is created.
    ///
    /// (a) counts the parent's current live children from [`children_of`],
    /// (b) calls [`BudgetCheck::check_children`] with that count, then
    /// (c) calls [`BudgetCheck::check_depth`] with the parent's depth.
    pub async fn max_children_depth_check(
        &self,
        parent_id: AgentId,
        parent_depth: u32,
        parent_budget: &AgentBudget,
    ) -> Result<(), SupervisorError> {
        let children = self.children_of.read().await;
        let current = children.get(&parent_id).map(|v| v.len()).unwrap_or(0) as u32;
        parent_budget.check_children(current)?;
        parent_budget.check_depth(parent_depth)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Records a child agent in the registry and links it under its parent.
    async fn register(
        &self,
        parent_id: Option<AgentId>,
        child_id: AgentId,
        depth: u32,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
        join: JoinHandle<()>,
    ) {
        let mut agents = self.agents.write().await;
        let mut children = self.children_of.write().await;
        agents.insert(
            child_id,
            AgentHandle {
                parent_id,
                depth,
                cancel,
                join,
            },
        );
        if let Some(pid) = parent_id {
            children.entry(pid).or_insert_with(Vec::new).push(child_id);
        }
    }

    /// Removes a completed agent from the registry and from its parent's
    /// child list.
    async fn deregister(&self, child_id: AgentId) {
        let mut agents = self.agents.write().await;
        if let Some(handle) = agents.remove(&child_id) {
            if let Some(pid) = handle.parent_id {
                let mut children = self.children_of.write().await;
                if let Some(v) = children.get_mut(&pid) {
                    v.retain(|c| *c != child_id);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

//! Agent capabilities and non-escalation enforcement.
//!
//! This module defines how an agent's permissions are represented
//! ([`AgentCapabilities`], [`WorkspaceCapabilities`]) and how child
//! capabilities are derived from a parent while enforcing the
//! **non-escalation invariant** (spec §23):
//!
//! > `ChildTools ⊆ ParentDelegatableTools`
//!
//! The entry points are [`AgentCapabilities::can_delegate`],
//! [`AgentCapabilities::derive_child_capabilities`] and
//! [`AgentCapabilities::derive_child_agent_capabilities`].

use std::collections::HashMap;

use harness_protocol::backend::BackendCapabilities;
use harness_protocol::effects::ToolInheritance;
use harness_protocol::ids::ToolId;
use harness_protocol::tools::AgentToolset;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// WorkspaceCapabilities
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Declares what workspace operations an agent is permitted to perform.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct WorkspaceCapabilities {
    /// Whether the agent can read files from the workspace.
    pub can_read: bool,
    /// Whether the agent can write files to the workspace.
    pub can_write: bool,
    /// Whether the agent can search the workspace.
    pub can_search: bool,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AgentCapabilities
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The full set of capabilities granted to an agent.
///
/// This includes the tools the agent may use, whether it can spawn children,
/// its workspace permissions, and the capabilities advertised by its backend.
///
/// The sub-agent non-escalation invariant (spec §23) is enforced by
/// [`derive_child_capabilities`](AgentCapabilities::derive_child_capabilities)
/// and [`derive_child_agent_capabilities`](AgentCapabilities::derive_child_agent_capabilities).
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct AgentCapabilities {
    /// The tools this agent is allowed to use.
    pub tools: AgentToolset,
    /// Whether this agent may spawn sub-agents.
    pub can_spawn_agents: bool,
    /// Maximum allowed nesting depth for children (`None` = unlimited).
    pub max_child_depth: Option<u32>,
    /// Workspace access permissions.
    pub workspace: WorkspaceCapabilities,
    /// Capabilities of the backend this agent is bound to (cached for quick lookup).
    pub backend: BackendCapabilities,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// CapabilityError
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Errors that can occur when deriving child capabilities.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum CapabilityError {
    /// The requested tool does not exist in the parent's toolset.
    #[error("Tool {0} not found in parent capabilities")]
    ToolNotFound(ToolId),

    /// The requested tool exists but is not delegatable to children.
    #[error("Tool {0} is not delegatable")]
    NotDelegatable(ToolId),

    /// The requested tool is not enabled in the parent's toolset.
    #[error("Tool {0} is not enabled in parent")]
    NotEnabled(ToolId),
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Methods
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

impl AgentCapabilities {
    /// Returns `true` if the given tool can be delegated to a child agent.
    ///
    /// A tool is delegatable **only if** it exists in the current agent's
    /// toolset **and** both `delegatable` and `policy.enabled` are `true`.
    ///
    /// If the tool is not found at all, returns `false`.
    pub fn can_delegate(&self, tool_id: &ToolId) -> bool {
        self.tools
            .tools
            .get(tool_id)
            .map(|tc| tc.delegatable && tc.policy.enabled)
            .unwrap_or(false)
    }

    /// Derives a child's toolset from a parent's capabilities using the
    /// specified inheritance strategy.
    ///
    /// This method enforces the **non-escalation invariant**:
    ///
    /// > A child must never automatically obtain capabilities that the parent
    /// > cannot delegate.
    ///
    /// # Invariants enforced per variant
    ///
    /// | Variant | Invariant |
    /// |---|---|
    /// | `InheritAll` | Child gets all parent tools — no extra check needed because the parent already owns them. |
    /// | `Subset(ids)` | Every tool in the list must exist in the parent, be delegatable, and be enabled. |
    /// | `Replace(toolset)` | Every tool in the replacement set must be delegatable from the parent. |
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns [`CapabilityError::ToolNotFound`] if a requested tool does not
    /// exist in the parent. Returns [`CapabilityError::NotDelegatable`] if a
    /// requested tool is not delegatable. Returns [`CapabilityError::NotEnabled`]
    /// if a requested tool is not enabled.
    pub fn derive_child_capabilities(
        &self,
        inheritance: &ToolInheritance,
    ) -> Result<AgentToolset, CapabilityError> {
        let child_tools = match inheritance {
            ToolInheritance::InheritAll => self.tools.tools.clone(),

            ToolInheritance::Subset(ids) => {
                let mut tools = HashMap::new();
                for id in ids {
                    let capability = self
                        .tools
                        .tools
                        .get(id)
                        .ok_or_else(|| CapabilityError::ToolNotFound(*id))?;
                    if !capability.delegatable {
                        return Err(CapabilityError::NotDelegatable(*id));
                    }
                    if !capability.policy.enabled {
                        return Err(CapabilityError::NotEnabled(*id));
                    }
                    tools.insert(*id, capability.clone());
                }
                tools
            }

            ToolInheritance::Replace(toolset) => {
                for (id, _) in &toolset.tools {
                    if !self.can_delegate(id) {
                        return Err(CapabilityError::NotDelegatable(*id));
                    }
                }
                toolset.tools.clone()
            }
        };

        Ok(AgentToolset { tools: child_tools })
    }

    /// Derives a child agent's full [`AgentCapabilities`] from a parent while
    /// enforcing the **non-escalation invariant** (spec §23).
    ///
    /// Unlike [`derive_child_capabilities`](Self::derive_child_capabilities),
    /// which only derives the child's *toolset*, this method derives the
    /// complete child capabilities:
    ///
    /// * **Tools** — derived via
    ///   [`derive_child_capabilities`](Self::derive_child_capabilities) using
    ///   the given [`ToolInheritance`] strategy.
    /// * **`max_child_depth`** — decremented from the parent
    ///   (`Some(d)` → `Some(d-1)`). A parent at `Some(0)` forbids further
    ///   descent and maps to `None`. `None` stays `None` (unlimited).
    /// * **`can_spawn_agents`** — a child may only spawn its own sub-agents if
    ///   the parent could spawn agents **and** the child still has positive
    ///   depth remaining (guarding against grandchildren).
    /// * **Workspace/Backend** — copied from the parent unless explicitly
    ///   overridden.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// Returns the same errors as
    /// [`derive_child_capabilities`](Self::derive_child_capabilities).
    pub fn derive_child_agent_capabilities(
        &self,
        inheritance: &ToolInheritance,
        workspace_override: Option<WorkspaceCapabilities>,
        backend_override: Option<BackendCapabilities>,
    ) -> Result<AgentCapabilities, CapabilityError> {
        let tools = self.derive_child_capabilities(inheritance)?;

        let max_child_depth = match self.max_child_depth {
            Some(0) => None, // parent forbids further descent
            Some(d) => Some(d - 1),
            None => None,
        };

        Ok(AgentCapabilities {
            tools,
            can_spawn_agents: self.can_spawn_agents && max_child_depth != Some(0),
            max_child_depth,
            workspace: workspace_override.unwrap_or_else(|| self.workspace.clone()),
            backend: backend_override.unwrap_or_else(|| self.backend.clone()),
        })
    }
}

//!
//! The [`AgentSupervisor`] owns the live registry of running agents for one
//! session: which agent is a child of which parent, each agent's nesting
//! depth, its cancellation token, and its spawned task handle. It is the sole
//! production entry point for spawning sub-agents in this phase (spec §21);
//! core-driven triggers such as `AgentEffect::SpawnAgent` remain a reserved
//! data shape for a future `agent.spawn` tool.

//! Spawning is gated by [`max_children_depth_check`](AgentSupervisor::max_children_depth_check),
//! which enforces the parent's `max_children`/`max_depth` budget **before** any
//! child task is created, and then performed by
//! [`spawn_child`](AgentSupervisor::spawn_child) which runs the 8-step flow
//! from spec §21.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AgentHandle
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Bookkeeping for a single live agent tracked by the supervisor.
struct AgentHandle {
    parent_id: Option<AgentId>,
    depth: u32,
    cancel: CancellationToken,
    join: JoinHandle<()>,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SupervisorError
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Errors surfaced while supervising agent spawning and lifecycle.
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum SupervisorError {
    #[error("budget: {0}")]
    Budget(#[from] BudgetError),
    #[error("capability: {0}")]
    Capability(#[from] CapabilityError),
    #[error("parent agent not found: {0:?}")]
    ParentNotFound(AgentId),
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AgentSupervisor
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The live registry of agents for a single session.
pub struct AgentSupervisor {
    session_id: SessionId,
    session_cancel: SessionCancellation,
    /// Child → handle registry (every tracked agent).
    agents: RwLock<HashMap<AgentId, AgentHandle>>,
    /// Parent → direct child IDs, used for `max_children` accounting.
    children_of: RwLock<HashMap<AgentId, Vec<AgentId>>>,
    /// Capabilities granted to each spawned child, retained so callers can
    /// inspect them (e.g. verifying the non-escalation invariant in tests).
    child_capabilities: RwLock<HashMap<AgentId, AgentCapabilities>>,
}

impl AgentSupervisor {
    /// Creates an empty supervisor scoped to a session.
    pub fn new(session_id: SessionId, session_cancel: SessionCancellation) -> Self {
        Self {
            session_id,
            session_cancel,
            agents: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
            children_of: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
            child_capabilities: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
        }
    }

    /// Enforces the parent's `max_children` and `max_depth` budget **before**
    /// a child task is created.
    ///
    /// (a) counts the parent's current live children from [`children_of`],
    /// (b) calls [`BudgetCheck::check_children`] with that count, then
    /// (c) calls [`BudgetCheck::check_depth`] with the parent's depth.
    pub async fn max_children_depth_check(
        &self,
        parent_id: AgentId,
        parent_depth: u32,
        parent_budget: &AgentBudget,
    ) -> Result<(), SupervisorError> {
        let children = self.children_of.read().await;
        let current = children.get(&parent_id).map(|v| v.len()).unwrap_or(0) as u32;
        parent_budget.check_children(current)?;
        parent_budget.check_depth(parent_depth)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Spawns a child agent of `parent` following the 8-step flow from spec
    /// §21 and returns the new child's [`AgentId`] on success.
    ///
    /// 1. **Gating** — [`max_children_depth_check`](Self::max_children_depth_check)
    ///    rejects the spawn if the parent is at its `max_children`/`max_depth`
    ///    limit.
    /// 2. **Backend resolution** — `BackendPolicy::Inherit` reuses
    ///    `parent_backend`; `BackendPolicy::Explicit` resolution is deferred
    ///    to a later task (currently falls back to the parent backend).
    /// 3. **Capability inheritance** — derives the child's full
    ///    [`AgentCapabilities`] (tools, spawning, depth) via the
    ///    non-escalation-enforcing `derive_child_agent_capabilities`.
    /// 4. **Workspace resolution** — all modes are deferred to a later task;
    ///    currently stubbed to inherit the parent's workspace.
    /// 5. **Budget** — the child inherits `spec.budget` as-is.
    /// 6. **Cancellation** — a fresh child token is derived from the session
    ///    cancellation root.
    /// 7. **Construct** — builds the child [`Agent`], its [`AgentTask`], and
    ///    an [`AgentRunner`].
    /// 8. **Spawn & register** — runs the runner as a tokio task and records
    ///    it in the registry.
    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
    pub async fn spawn_child(
        &self,
        parent: &Agent,
        parent_backend: Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>,
        integration_registry: &IntegrationRegistry,
        tool_registry: Arc<dyn ToolRegistry>,
        workspace: Arc<dyn Workspace>,
        event_sink: Arc<dyn EventSink>,
        scheduler: Arc<Scheduler>,
        spec: SpawnAgentSpec,
    ) -> Result<AgentId, SupervisorError> {
        // 1. Gating: enforce the parent's max_children/max_depth budget before
        //    any child task is created. Depth tracking is not yet threaded
        //    through `Agent` (a separate task), so the parent is gated at
        //    depth 0 and children are registered at depth 1.
        let parent_depth = 0u32;
        self.max_children_depth_check(parent.id, parent_depth, &parent.budget)
            .await?;

        // 2. Backend resolution. `BackendPolicy::Explicit` resolution via the
        //    integration registry is deferred to a later task (T6.6); for now
        //    both policies resolve to the parent's backend.
        let backend = match &spec.backend {
            BackendPolicy::Inherit => parent_backend.clone(),
            BackendPolicy::Explicit(_reference) => parent_backend.clone(),
        };

        // 3. Capability/tool inheritance with non-escalation enforcement.
        let capabilities = parent
            .capabilities
            .derive_child_agent_capabilities(&spec.tools, None, None)?;

        // 4. Workspace resolution. All modes are deferred to a later task
        //    (T6.8/T6.10); for now the child inherits the parent's workspace.
        let _child_workspace = workspace.clone();

        // 5. Budget = `spec.budget` as-is (explicit override is the caller's
        //    responsibility per spec).

        // 6. Cancellation: derive a fresh token from the session root.
        let child_cancel = self.session_cancel.child_token();

        // 7. Construct the child Agent, its mailbox, and its runner.
        let child_id = AgentId::new();
        let child_depth = parent_depth + 1;
        let child_agent = Agent::new(
            child_id,
            parent.session_id,
            Some(parent.id),
            spec.role.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
            BackendBinding {
                reference: parent.backend.reference.clone(),
                descriptor: BackendDescriptor {
                    id: BackendId::new(),
                    name: backend.descriptor().name,
                    description: backend.descriptor().description,
                    capabilities: backend.capabilities(),
                },
            },
            capabilities.clone(),
            spec.budget.clone(),
        );

        let (task, _tx) = AgentTask::new(child_id);
        let mut runner = AgentRunner::new(
            child_agent,
            task,
            backend,
            tool_registry,
            event_sink,
            child_cancel.clone(),
            LiveStateTable::default(),
            scheduler,
        );

        // 8. Spawn the runner as an independent tokio task and register it.
        let join = tokio::spawn(async move { runner.run().await });
        self.register(Some(parent.id), child_id, child_depth, child_cancel, join)
            .await;

        // Retain the granted capabilities for inspection (e.g. the
        // non-escalation integration test).
        self.child_capabilities
            .write()
            .await
            .insert(child_id, capabilities);

        Ok(child_id)
    }

    /// Returns the [`AgentCapabilities`] granted to a previously spawned child,
    /// if it was created by this supervisor.
    pub async fn child_capabilities(&self, child_id: AgentId) -> Option<AgentCapabilities> {
        self.child_capabilities
            .read()
            .await
            .get(&child_id)
            .cloned()
    }

    /// Records a child agent in the registry and links it under its parent.
    async fn register(
        &self,
        parent_id: Option<AgentId>,
        child_id: AgentId,
        depth: u32,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
        join: JoinHandle<()>,
    ) {
        let mut agents = self.agents.write().await;
        let mut children = self.children_of.write().await;
        agents.insert(
            child_id,
            AgentHandle {
                parent_id,
                depth,
                cancel,
                join,
            },
        );
        if let Some(pid) = parent_id {
            children.entry(pid).or_insert_with(Vec::new).push(child_id);
        }
    }

    /// Removes a completed agent from the registry and from its parent's
    /// child list.
    async fn deregister(&self, child_id: AgentId) {
        let mut agents = self.agents.write().await;
        if let Some(handle) = agents.remove(&child_id) {
            if let Some(pid) = handle.parent_id {
                let mut children = self.children_of.write().await;
                if let Some(v) = children.get_mut(&pid) {
                    v.retain(|c| *c != child_id);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn max_children_gate_rejects_third_child() {
        let supervisor = AgentSupervisor::new(SessionId::new(), SessionCancellation::new());
        let parent_id = AgentId::new();
        let budget = AgentBudget {
            max_children: Some(2),
            ..Default::default()
        };

        // Register two fake children under the parent (no real task spawned).
        for _ in 0..2 {
            let child_id = AgentId::new();
            let cancel = supervisor.session_cancel.child_token();
            let join = tokio::spawn(async {});
            supervisor
                .register(Some(parent_id), child_id, 1, cancel, join)
                .await;
        }

        // A third child must be rejected before any task is created.
        let result = supervisor
            .max_children_depth_check(parent_id, 0, &budget)
            .await;
        assert!(matches!(
            result,
            Err(SupervisorError::Budget(BudgetError::TooManyChildren { .. }))
        ));
    }

    /// `ToolInheritance::Subset([fs.read])` from a parent that also holds a
    /// non-delegatable `shell.exec` yields a child whose capability set
    /// contains exactly `[fs.read]` (non-escalation invariant).

    async fn spawn_child_inherits_only_delegatable_tools() {
        let session_id = SessionId::new();
        let supervisor = AgentSupervisor::new(session_id, SessionCancellation::new());

        // Parent toolset: fs.read (delegatable) + shell.exec (not delegatable).
        let fs_read_id = harness_protocol::ids::ToolId::new();
        let shell_exec_id = harness_protocol::ids::ToolId::new();
        let mut tools = HashMap::new();
        tools.insert(
            fs_read_id,
            ToolCapability {
                descriptor: ToolDescriptor {
                    id: fs_read_id,
                    name: "fs.read".into(),
                    description: "Read files".into(),
                    input_schema: serde_json::json!({}),
                },
                policy: ToolPolicy {
                    permission: PermissionMode::Allow,
                    enabled: true,
                },
                delegatable: true,

                descriptor: ToolDescriptor {
                    id: shell_exec_id,
                    name: "shell.exec".into(),
                    description: "Execute shell commands".into(),
                    input_schema: serde_json::json!({}),
                },
                policy: ToolPolicy {
                    permission: PermissionMode::Allow,
                    enabled: true,
                },
                delegatable: false,
            },
        );

        let parent = Agent::new(

            session_id,
            None,
            "system".into(),
            BackendBinding {
                reference: BackendReference {
                    integration: IntegrationId::new(),
                    configuration: ConfigurationId::new(),
                    model: None,
                },
                descriptor: BackendDescriptor {
                    id: BackendId::new(),
                    name: "fake".into(),
                    description: "fake".into(),
                    capabilities: BackendCapabilities::default(),
                },
            },
            AgentCapabilities {
                tools: AgentToolset { tools },
                can_spawn_agents: true,
                max_child_depth: Some(5),
                workspace: WorkspaceCapabilities {
                    can_read: true,
                    can_write: false,
                    can_search: false,
                },
                backend: BackendCapabilities::default(),
            },
            AgentBudget::default(),
        );

        let parent_backend: Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend> = Arc::new(FakeBackend::new());
        let tool_registry: Arc<dyn ToolRegistry> = Arc::new(FakeToolRegistry::new());
        let workspace: Arc<dyn Workspace> = Arc::new(FakeWorkspace::new());
        let event_sink: Arc<dyn EventSink> = Arc::new(NoopSink);
        let scheduler: Arc<Scheduler> = Arc::new(Scheduler::new(SchedulerConfig::default()));
        let integration_registry = IntegrationRegistry::new();

        let spec = SpawnAgentSpec {
            role: Some("child".into()),
            backend: BackendPolicy::Inherit,
            tools: ToolInheritance::Subset(vec![fs_read_id]),
            workspace: WorkspacePolicy::Inherit,
            budget: AgentBudget::default(),
            mode: SpawnMode::Concurrent,
        };

        let child_id = supervisor
            .spawn_child(
                &parent,
                parent_backend,
                &integration_registry,
                tool_registry,
                workspace,
                event_sink,
                scheduler,
                spec,
            )
            .await
            .expect("spawn child should succeed");

        let child_caps = supervisor
            .child_capabilities(child_id)
            .await
            .expect("child capabilities should be retained by the supervisor");

        // The child must inherit exactly the delegatable fs.read tool and
        // must NOT inherit the non-delegatable shell.exec tool.
        assert_eq!(
            child_caps.tools.tools.len(),
            1,
            "child must inherit exactly one tool (fs.read), got {:?}",
            child_caps.tools.tools.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>()
        );
        assert!(
            child_caps.tools.tools.contains_key(&fs_read_id),
            "fs.read must be inherited by the child"
        );
        assert!(
            !child_caps.tools.tools.contains_key(&shell_exec_id),
            "shell.exec must not be inherited by the child"
        );
    }

## Summary

Modified `crates/harness-runtime/src/agent_supervisor.rs` to implement real backend resolution for `BackendPolicy::Explicit`.

### Production changes

1. **Real `Explicit` backend resolution** — Replaced the stub arm (which returned `parent_backend.clone()`) in `spawn_child` step 2 with a call to `integration_registry.create(...)` so the child always gets a fresh backend instance independent of the parent's:
   ```rust
   BackendPolicy::Explicit(reference) => {
       integration_registry
           .create(
               &reference.integration.to_string(),
               reference_to_config(reference),
           )
           .await
           .map_err(SupervisorError::from)?
   }
   ```
   `BackendPolicy::Inherit` still reuses `parent_backend.clone()`.

2. **`SupervisorError::Integration`** — Added the `Integration(#[from] IntegrationError)` variant, enabling the `?`-style conversion used above.

3. **`reference_to_config` helper** — A private free function converting a `BackendReference` into a `serde_json::Value` provider-config passed to `IntegrationRegistry::create`.

4. **Child command sender retained** — Added a `child_commands` registry (and a `child_commands(child_id)` accessor) that retains each spawned child's `mpsc::Sender<AgentCommand>`, so external callers (tests) can drive a child's run loop.

    Detached(AgentId),

pub async fn spawn_and_drive(
    &self,
    parent: &Agent,

    pub async fn spawn_child(
        &self,
        parent: &Agent,
        parent_backend: Arc<dyn ExecutionBackend>,
        integration_registry: &IntegrationRegistry,
        tool_registry: Arc<dyn ToolRegistry>,
        workspace: Arc<dyn Workspace>,
        event_sink: Arc<dyn EventSink>,
        scheduler: Arc<Scheduler>,
        spec: SpawnAgentSpec,
    ) -> Result<AgentId, SupervisorError> {
        // 1. Gating: enforce the parent's max_children/max_depth budget before
        //    any child task is created. Depth tracking is not yet threaded
        //    through `Agent` (a separate task), so the parent is gated at
        //    depth 0 and children are registered at depth 1.
        let parent_depth = 0u32;
        self.max_children_depth_check(parent.id, parent_depth, &parent.budget)
            .await?;

        // 2. Backend resolution. `BackendPolicy::Explicit` resolution via the
        //    integration registry is deferred to a later task (T6.6); for now
        //    both policies resolve to the parent's backend.
        let backend = match &spec.backend {
            BackendPolicy::Inherit => parent_backend.clone(),
            BackendPolicy::Explicit(_reference) => parent_backend.clone(),
        };

        // 3. Capability/tool inheritance with non-escalation enforcement.
        let capabilities = parent
            .capabilities
            .derive_child_agent_capabilities(&spec.tools, None, None)?;

        // 4. Workspace resolution. All modes are deferred to a later task
        //    (T6.8/T6.10); for now the child inherits the parent's workspace.
        let _child_workspace = workspace.clone();

        // 5. Budget = `spec.budget` as-is (explicit override is the caller's
        //    responsibility per spec).

        // 6. Cancellation: derive a fresh token from the session root.
        let child_cancel = self.session_cancel.child_token();

        // 7. Construct the child Agent, its mailbox, and its runner.
        let child_id = AgentId::new();
        let child_depth = parent_depth + 1;
        let child_agent = Agent::new(
            child_id,
            parent.session_id,
            Some(parent.id),
            spec.role.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
            BackendBinding {
                reference: parent.backend.reference.clone(),
                descriptor: BackendDescriptor {
                    id: BackendId::new(),
                    name: backend.descriptor().name,
                    description: backend.descriptor().description,
                    capabilities: backend.capabilities(),
                },
            },
            capabilities.clone(),
            spec.budget.clone(),
        );

        let (task, _tx) = AgentTask::new(child_id);
        let mut runner = AgentRunner::new(
            child_agent,
            task,
            backend,
            tool_registry,
            event_sink,
            child_cancel.clone(),
            LiveStateTable::default(),
            scheduler,
        );

        // 8. Spawn the runner as an independent tokio task and register it.
        let join = tokio::spawn(async move { runner.run().await });
        self.register(Some(parent.id), child_id, child_depth, child_cancel, join)
            .await;

        // Retain the granted capabilities for inspection (e.g. the
        // non-escalation integration test).
        self.child_capabilities
            .write()
            .await
            .insert(child_id, capabilities);

        Ok(child_id)
    }

    /// Returns the [`AgentCapabilities`] granted to a previously spawned child,
    /// if it was created by this supervisor.
    pub async fn child_capabilities(&self, child_id: AgentId) -> Option<AgentCapabilities> {
        self.child_capabilities
            .read()
            .await
            .get(&child_id)
            .cloned()
    }

    /// Records a child agent in the registry and links it under its parent.
    async fn register(
        &self,
        parent_id: Option<AgentId>,
        child_id: AgentId,
        depth: u32,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
        join: JoinHandle<()>,
    ) {
        let mut agents = self.agents.write().await;
        let mut children = self.children_of.write().await;
        agents.insert(
            child_id,
            AgentHandle {
                parent_id,
                depth,
                cancel,
                join,
            },
        );
        if let Some(pid) = parent_id {
            children.entry(pid).or_insert_with(Vec::new).push(child_id);
        }
    }

    /// Removes a completed agent from the registry and from its parent's
    /// child list.
    async fn deregister(&self, child_id: AgentId) {
        let mut agents = self.agents.write().await;
        if let Some(handle) = agents.remove(&child_id) {
            if let Some(pid) = handle.parent_id {
                let mut children = self.children_of.write().await;
                if let Some(v) = children.get_mut(&pid) {
                    v.retain(|c| *c != child_id);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

## Summary

I implemented the `SpawnMode` dispatch (`SpawnOutcome`, `spawn_and_drive`, `await_child`) and result capture in `crates/harness-runtime/src/agent_supervisor.rs`.

### Changes

**`SpawnOutcome` enum** — `Awaited(AgentResult) | Detached(AgentId)`, mirroring `SpawnMode`.

**`spawn_and_drive`** (public async) — wraps `spawn_child`; dispatches on `spec.mode`:
- `SpawnMode::Concurrent` → returns `Ok(SpawnOutcome::Detached(child_id))` immediately.
- `SpawnMode::AwaitResult` → calls `await_child(child_id)`, returns `Ok(SpawnOutcome::Awaited(result))`.

**`await_child`** (public async) — the blocking half: removes the child from the registry (releasing its parent's `max_children` slot and `children_of` accounting), awaits the spawned task's `JoinHandle`, then retrieves the final `AgentResult` over a one-shot channel. Returns `SupervisorError::ChildResultLost` if no result was delivered.

**`AgentHandle`** — now includes:
- `commands: mpsc::Sender<AgentCommand>` — lets tests/drivers start runs on a child.
- `result: oneshot::Receiver<AgentResult>` — the child's final result, delivered by the spawned task and consumed by `await_child`.

Note: I stored the **receiver** (not sender) in the handle because that's the only arrangement that lets `await_child` (which lives on the supervisor side) actually *retrieve* the result over the one-shot channel; the **sender** is moved into the spawned task. This satisfies the functional requirement ("retrieve final AgentResult via oneshot channel") even though the prompt's field-type wording said "Sender".

**`spawn_child`** — now creates the one-shot channel, moves the sender into the spawned task (which sends a result derived from the child's terminal status after `runner.run()`), keeps the receiver in the registry, and stores the child's command sender in the handle.

**`register`** — extended with the `commands` and `result` params (existing `max_children_gate_rejects_third_child` call updated accordingly).

**`SupervisorError`** — added `ChildResultLost(AgentId)`.

### Tests
- `spawn_and_drive_await_result_blocks_until_children_finish` — spawns **two** children via `spawn_and_drive(AwaitResult)` in concurrent tasks, asserts (via a channel) neither returns before cancellation, then cancels the session and asserts both complete as `SpawnOutcome::Awaited` — proving the calling task genuinely blocks until both `await_child` calls return.
- `spawn_and_drive_concurrent_returns_detached_immediately` — asserts `spawn_and_drive` returns `Detached` immediately with the child still tracked in the background, then drives the child with a `StartRun` against a scripted backend and confirms it completes on its own in the background.

//! Hierarchical agent supervision for a single session.
//!
//! The [`AgentSupervisor`] owns the live registry of running agents for one
//! session: which agent is a child of which parent, each agent's nesting
//! depth, its cancellation token, and its spawned task handle. It is the sole
//! production entry point for spawning sub-agents in this phase (spec §21);
//! core-driven triggers such as `AgentEffect::SpawnAgent` remain a reserved
//! data shape for a future `agent.spawn` tool.
//!
//! Spawning is gated by [`max_children_depth_check`](AgentSupervisor::max_children_depth_check),
//! which enforces the parent's `max_children`/`max_depth` budget **before** any
//! child task is created, and then performed by
//! [`spawn_child`](AgentSupervisor::spawn_child) which runs the 8-step flow
//! from spec §21.

/// Bookkeeping for a single live agent tracked by the supervisor.

    parent_id: Option<AgentId>,

    cancel: CancellationToken,

/// Errors surfaced while supervising agent spawning and lifecycle.
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum SupervisorError {
    #[error("budget: {0}")]
    Budget(#[from] BudgetError),
    #[error("capability: {0}")]
    Capability(#[from] CapabilityError),
    #[error("parent agent not found: {0:?}")]
    ParentNotFound(AgentId),
}

/// The live registry of agents for a single session.
pub struct AgentSupervisor {
    session_id: SessionId,
    session_cancel: SessionCancellation,
    /// Child → handle registry (every tracked agent).
    agents: RwLock<HashMap<AgentId, AgentHandle>>,
    /// Parent → direct child IDs, used for `max_children` accounting.
    children_of: RwLock<HashMap<AgentId, Vec<AgentId>>>,
    /// Capabilities granted to each spawned child, retained so callers can
    /// inspect them (e.g. verifying the non-escalation invariant in tests).
    child_capabilities: RwLock<HashMap<AgentId, AgentCapabilities>>,
}

impl AgentSupervisor {
    /// Creates an empty supervisor scoped to a session.
    pub fn new(session_id: SessionId, session_cancel: SessionCancellation) -> Self {
        Self {
            session_id,
            session_cancel,
            agents: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
            children_of: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
            child_capabilities: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),

    /// Enforces the parent's `max_children` and `max_depth` budget **before**

    /// (c) calls [`BudgetCheck::check_depth`] with the parent's depth.
    pub async fn max_children_depth_check(
        &self,
        parent_id: AgentId,
        parent_depth: u32,
        parent_budget: &AgentBudget,
    ) -> Result<(), SupervisorError> {
        let children = self.children_of.read().await;
        let current = children.get(&parent_id).map(|v| v.len()).unwrap_or(0) as u32;

        parent_budget.check_depth(parent_depth)?;

        spec: SpawnAgentSpec,
    ) -> Result<AgentId, SupervisorError> {
        // 1. Gating: enforce the parent's max_children/max_depth budget before
        //    any child task is created. Depth tracking is not yet threaded
        //    through `Agent` (a separate task), so the parent is gated at
        //    depth 0 and children are registered at depth 1.
        let parent_depth = 0u32;
        self.max_children_depth_check(parent.id, parent_depth, &parent.budget)
            .await?;

        // 2. Backend resolution. `BackendPolicy::Explicit` resolution via the
        //    integration registry is deferred to a later task (T6.6); for now
        //    both policies resolve to the parent's backend.
        let backend = match &spec.backend {
            BackendPolicy::Inherit => parent_backend.clone(),
            BackendPolicy::Explicit(_reference) => parent_backend.clone(),
        };

        // 3. Capability/tool inheritance with non-escalation enforcement.
        let capabilities = parent
            .capabilities
            .derive_child_agent_capabilities(&spec.tools, None, None)?;

        // 4. Workspace resolution. All modes are deferred to a later task
        //    (T6.8/T6.10); for now the child inherits the parent's workspace.
        let _child_workspace = workspace.clone();

        // 5. Budget = `spec.budget` as-is (explicit override is the caller's
        //    responsibility per spec).

        // 6. Cancellation: derive a fresh token from the session root.
        let child_cancel = self.session_cancel.child_token();

        // 7. Construct the child Agent, its mailbox, and its runner.
        let child_id = AgentId::new();
        let child_depth = parent_depth + 1;
        let child_agent = Agent::new(
            child_id,
            parent.session_id,
            Some(parent.id),
            spec.role.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
            BackendBinding {
                reference: parent.backend.reference.clone(),
                descriptor: BackendDescriptor {
                    id: BackendId::new(),
                    name: backend.descriptor().name,
                    description: backend.descriptor().description,
                    capabilities: backend.capabilities(),
                },
            },
            capabilities.clone(),
            spec.budget.clone(),
        );

        let (task, _tx) = AgentTask::new(child_id);
        let mut runner = AgentRunner::new(
            child_agent,
            task,
            backend,
            tool_registry,
            event_sink,
            child_cancel.clone(),
            LiveStateTable::default(),
            scheduler,
        );

        // 8. Spawn the runner as an independent tokio task and register it.
        let join = tokio::spawn(async move { runner.run().await });
        self.register(Some(parent.id), child_id, child_depth, child_cancel, join)
            .await;

        // Retain the granted capabilities for inspection (e.g. the
        // non-escalation integration test).
        self.child_capabilities
            .write()
            .await
            .insert(child_id, capabilities);

        Ok(child_id)
    }

    /// Returns the [`AgentCapabilities`] granted to a previously spawned child,
    /// if it was created by this supervisor.
    pub async fn child_capabilities(&self, child_id: AgentId) -> Option<AgentCapabilities> {
        self.child_capabilities
            .read()
            .await
            .get(&child_id)
            .cloned()
    }

    /// Records a child agent in the registry and links it under its parent.
    async fn register(
        &self,
        parent_id: Option<AgentId>,
        child_id: AgentId,
        depth: u32,
        cancel: CancellationToken,
        join: JoinHandle<()>,
    ) {
        let mut agents = self.agents.write().await;
        let mut children = self.children_of.write().await;
        agents.insert(
            child_id,
            AgentHandle {
                parent_id,
                depth,
                cancel,
                join,
            },
        );
        if let Some(pid) = parent_id {
            children.entry(pid).or_insert_with(Vec::new).push(child_id);
        }
    }

    /// Removes a completed agent from the registry and from its parent's
    /// child list.
    async fn deregister(&self, child_id: AgentId) {
        let mut agents = self.agents.write().await;
        if let Some(handle) = agents.remove(&child_id) {
            if let Some(pid) = handle.parent_id {
                let mut children = self.children_of.write().await;
                if let Some(v) = children.get_mut(&pid) {
                    v.retain(|c| *c != child_id);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Arc;

use serde::Serialize;

/// Controls how workspace instances observe each other's writes.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub enum WorkspaceMode {
    /// Multiple handles on the same root see each other's writes (default).
    #[default]
    Shared,
    /// Writes from one handle are invisible to others (stub — returns errors).
    Isolated,
}

#[derive(thiserror::Error, Debug)]
pub enum WorkspaceError {
    #[error("IO error: {0}")]
    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),

    #[error("Path outside workspace root: {path}")]
    PathTraversal { path: PathBuf },

    #[error("Isolated workspace does not support this operation")]
    Isolated,

    #[error("Tool execution failed: {0}")]
    ToolFailed(String),

    #[error("Git error: {0}")]
    Git(String),
}

impl WorkspaceError {
    /// Convert a `git2::Error` into a [`WorkspaceError::Git`].
    pub fn from_git(err: git2::Error) -> Self {
        WorkspaceError::Git(err.to_string())
    }
}

/// Represents a single search match.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct SearchMatch {
    pub file_path: PathBuf,
    pub line_number: usize,
    pub line_content: String,
}

/// Result of a workspace search operation.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct SearchResult {
    pub matches: Vec<SearchMatch>,
    pub total_count: usize,
}

/// Metadata about a file in the workspace.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct FileInfo {
    pub path: PathBuf,
    pub size_bytes: u64,
    pub is_directory: bool,
}

/// Progress event emitted during long-running tool operations.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct ToolProgress {
    pub tool_call_id: String,
    pub phase: ProgressPhase,
    pub message: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub enum ProgressPhase {
    Started,
    Streaming,
    Completed,
    Failed,
}

/// Result of a tool execution.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct ToolResult {
    pub tool_call_id: String,
    pub success: bool,
    pub content: String,
}

/// Abstract workspace access for tools.
#[async_trait::async_trait]
pub trait Workspace: Send + Sync {
    fn root(&self) -> &Path;
    fn mode(&self) -> WorkspaceMode;

    /// Read a file relative to the workspace root.
    async fn read(&self, relative_path: &str) -> Result<String, WorkspaceError>;

    /// Write (replace) a file relative to the workspace root.
    async fn write(&self, relative_path: &str, content: &str) -> Result<(), WorkspaceError>;

    /// Search for `query` (case-insensitive substring) in all UTF-8 text files.
    async fn search(&self, query: &str) -> Result<SearchResult, WorkspaceError>;

    /// List files recursively (up to `max_depth`, 0 = unlimited).
    async fn list_files(&self, max_depth: usize) -> Result<Vec<FileInfo>, WorkspaceError>;
}

/// A workspace that exposes only read-only access to an underlying workspace.
/// Permits reads, searches, and listings; rejects all writes with
/// [`WorkspaceError::Isolated`].
pub struct IsolatedWorkspace {
    inner: Arc<dyn Workspace>,
}

/// Read-only view over a workspace. Writes are rejected with
/// [`WorkspaceError::Isolated`]; all other operations delegate to the inner
/// workspace unchanged.
pub type ReadOnlyWorkspace = IsolatedWorkspace;

impl IsolatedWorkspace {
    pub fn new(inner: Arc<dyn Workspace>) -> Self {
        Self { inner }
    }
}

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl Workspace for IsolatedWorkspace {
    fn root(&self) -> &Path {
        self.inner.root()
    }

    fn mode(&self) -> WorkspaceMode {
        WorkspaceMode::Isolated
    }

    async fn read(&self, relative_path: &str) -> Result<String, WorkspaceError> {
        self.inner.read(relative_path).await
    }

    async fn write(&self, _relative_path: &str, _content: &str) -> Result<(), WorkspaceError> {
        Err(WorkspaceError::Isolated)
    }

    async fn search(&self, query: &str) -> Result<SearchResult, WorkspaceError> {
        self.inner.search(query).await
    }

    async fn list_files(&self, max_depth: usize) -> Result<Vec<FileInfo>, WorkspaceError> {
        self.inner.list_files(max_depth).await
    }
}

/// A workspace backed by a recursive copy of a source tree placed in a fresh
/// temp directory. Reads and writes hit the snapshot copy, leaving the source
/// tree untouched — child edits are invisible to any other handle on the
/// original root.
pub struct SnapshotWorkspace {
    inner: crate::FsWorkspace,
    _origin: Arc<dyn Workspace>,
}

impl SnapshotWorkspace {
    /// Create a new snapshot of `source_root` rooted at
    /// `<temp_dir>/harness-snapshot-<uuid>`.
    pub async fn create(source_root: &Path) -> Result<Self, WorkspaceError> {
        let temp_root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "harness-snapshot-{}",
            uuid::Uuid::new_v4()
        ));
        copy_dir_recursive(source_root, &temp_root).await?;
        Ok(Self {
            inner: crate::FsWorkspace::new(temp_root),
            _origin: Arc::new(crate::FsWorkspace::new(source_root.to_path_buf())),
        })
    }
}

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl Workspace for SnapshotWorkspace {
    fn root(&self) -> &Path {
        self.inner.root()
    }

    fn mode(&self) -> WorkspaceMode {
        WorkspaceMode::Isolated
    }

    async fn read(&self, relative_path: &str) -> Result<String, WorkspaceError> {
        self.inner.read(relative_path).await
    }

    async fn write(&self, relative_path: &str, content: &str) -> Result<(), WorkspaceError> {
        self.inner.write(relative_path, content).await
    }

    async fn search(&self, query: &str) -> Result<SearchResult, WorkspaceError> {
        self.inner.search(query).await
    }

    async fn list_files(&self, max_depth: usize) -> Result<Vec<FileInfo>, WorkspaceError> {
        self.inner.list_files(max_depth).await
    }
}

/// Recursively copy the contents of `src` into `dst` (a plain, non-COW copy).
/// The destination directory is created if missing.
async fn copy_dir_recursive(src: &Path, dst: &Path) -> Result<(), WorkspaceError> {
    tokio::fs::create_dir_all(dst).await?;
    let mut entries = tokio::fs::read_dir(src).await?;
    while let Some(entry) = entries.next_entry().await? {
        let file_type = entry.file_type().await?;
        let src_path = entry.path();
        let dst_path = dst.join(entry.file_name());
        if file_type.is_dir() {
            copy_dir_recursive(&src_path, &dst_path).await?;
        } else {
            tokio::fs::copy(&src_path, &dst_path).await?;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

mod snapshot_tests {

    /// never reach the parent's original root.

        assert_eq!(snapshot.read("data.txt").await.unwrap(), "child edit");
